The lower Nemunas linked settlements with routes toward the Baltic. Boats, crossings and bank roads were affected differently by water and season. People needed landings, provisions and passage agreements, and distant news could lag behind local changes. River guards watched vessels, bank access and night landings. Escorts protected goods while allowing crews to rest, often needing local boatmen in unfamiliar water.

Garrisons and river works needed resources, while households' supply varied seasonally.
